How does it promote the game?

 

by showing the extent of the card mechanic and hero abilities. Much of SotM complexity lies on the card text itself which you have no way of knowing from just reading the widely available rulebook. People on the fence of getting the game will love the chance to take a peek at the cards and just by imagining how a particular hero works, setting up potential combo, and see how it fits together thematically can easily drive SotM to a purchase!

In fact personally I bought Arkham Horror and Warhammer Invasion LCG after spending major amount of time looking at their cards spoiler and imagining how cool they will be when played.

Obviously for existing fans, looking at spoilers of a new expansion will easily persuade them on purchasing the new set too… Magic has done that for years with great effect.

posts.name: arenson9
posts.cooked:
I don't see how it could hurt anything. If all the text and art were available and someone wanted to print their own copy, it would probably cost more than just buying a set. Someone could just print the text or maybe print on flimsy cardstock or paper, but I doubt there would be enough people interested in doing so to seriously affect how many copies of the game are sold.

 

How could it help? Easier reference for online discussion would be nice. Showing off the cards might help some people decide they're interested in the game or an expansion.

 

As others have said, though, the main issue is who's willing to put the time and effort into making an easily-used online database of cards. I suppose GtGs might decide they're willing to post the proof sheets  at some point, but that's not particularly easy to use for referencing individual cards.
